claude.request:
Today's international headlines:
- How Arab parties could hold critical balance of power in Israeli election: Disaffection has often driven down turnout among Arab Israelis, but there is a strong push to get rid of the right-wing governing coalition.
- Governments working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning: Governments and companies are scrambling to protect their websites, as Amazon says it experienced attacks before the warning was made public.
- What is PHP and why did it spark a global cyber-security scramble?: AI uncovered long-hidden programming flaws, triggering a rare global cyber-security response.
- Missiles hit Kyiv after Russia agrees to US call to resume Ukraine peace talks: Moscow says it is "ready in principle" to resume peace talks and US President Donald Trump says the world is "the closest we've been" to ending the war.
- Rosenberg: US diplomatic push offers little hope for imminent Ukraine peace: President Vladimir Putin does not feel under pressure right now to end the war, the BBC's Russia Editor writes.
- US orders some diplomats to leave Saudi Arabia as Houthi attacks escalate: The warning to US officials comes as at least three people die in the latest strikes at an airport and an oil field.
- Airbnb hosts can no longer make guests strip beds and wash dishes under new rules: The updated policy will apply to all reservations booked on the accommodation site on or after 20 November.
- Macron accuses foreign leaders of exploiting French riots: The comment is an apparent swipe at Benjamin Netanyahu and Donald Trump, who both face elections in coming weeks.
- No order, no seat: Starbucks China rolls out new store policy: Starbucks says it is improving customers' in-store experience as it competes with homegrown rivals.
- US embassy accuses Canada of election meddling ahead of midterms: Prime Minister Mark Carney dismissed the claim, noting that it was the that US initiated trade actions against Canada.
- New Mexico sues Epstein lawyer and accountant, accusing them of hiding his sex crimes: Both men have denied having any knowledge of Epstein's crimes and their attorney rejected the lawsuit as "categorically false".
- Pope does not need further treatment after lung cancer surgery: Test results have confirmed his diagnosis as a lung adenocarcinoma that was localised.
